item.title: Summarizing Security Alerts on a Raspberry Pi, Part 1: Inference
item.description: Can a small language model explain security alerts on a Raspberry Pi 5, with nothing sent to the cloud? It can, but the runtime matters more than the model, and long prompts hurt some models much more than others. [14 min read]

item.title: Summarizing Security Alerts on a Raspberry Pi, Part 2: Fine-Tuning and Evaluation
item.description: This is the second part of our post about small language models for summarizing security alerts on a Raspberry Pi. Here we go into the details: how we fine-tuned the models, how we evaluated them, and a few things to keep in mind when deploying them. [9 min read]

item.title: Maybe it is time to focus on open LLMs for doing research?
item.description: The growing dependence on closed, inaccessible systems in academic publishing undermine the core principles of transparency, reproducibility, and openness. It is time to open models and community-driven innovation as the path forward for meaningful, equitable research. [3 min read]

item.title: Converting your own finetuned language model to GGUF
item.description: Sometimes your finetuned language Model work as expected but you need a faster inference time. Some other times you need to reduce memory footprint. By transformring your models to the GGUF format you can store quantized models and using them on top of the fast llama.cpp inference engine. [5 min read]
